title: First visit to a state
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine, let $q$ be a state, and let $c,d$ be configurations on a fixed Boolean input. Suppose every configuration whose state is $q$ is fixed by one step of $M$. If $d$ has state $q$ and running $M$ from $c$ for $T$ steps reaches $d$, then there is a time $t\le T$ at which the run from $c$ reaches $d$, and at every earlier time $j<t$ its state is different from $q$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $k$ of work tapes
A multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and state set $S$
Every configuration in state $q$ is fixed by one machine step
The run from $c$ for $T$ steps reaches $d$
